> And who knows, maybe @echasnovski 😉 will even temporarily use one of your logos if he likes the idea!

Yeah, I like the idea. My only concern was that this does not affect the repo itself (same as the current logo is tracked in Git). I can upload it to [`assets` repo](https://github.com/nvim-mini/assets) and temporarily (during holidays) link to it in the README as with standalone modules.

I have couple of questions:
- Would you mind just removing the blue dot behind tree's trunk? Everything else looks great.
- If you want to do the same for [MINI](https://github.com/nvim-mini/assets/blob/main/logo-2/logo-mini.png) and [MiniMax](https://github.com/nvim-mini/assets/blob/main/logo-2/logo-minimax_readme.png) logos, I'll do the same for them: MINI - on [site](https://nvim-mini.org/), MiniMax - in its README.

I think it is a bit too early to put them up. If you don't mind, I'll adjust them on December 1.

@drowning-cat, unfortunately for this discussion topic, the logos have now changed. They use vector graphics and are [autogenerated](https://github.com/nvim-mini/assets/blob/main/logo-3/generate.lua). Here is ['mini.nvim' one](https://github.com/nvim-mini/assets/blob/main/logo-3/logo-mini-nvim.svg?short_path=d2b2a59), for example.

I would love to keep using dedicated Christmas logos for 'mini.nvim', MINI, and MiniMax logos. It'd be better if they were also autogenerated from the code with preferably simple-ish `*.svg` as a result (i.e. no complex `path`, etc.). If you have any ideas, I'll take a look. If not, that's okay and I'll take a look sometime mid-November.

Not now, just something to reconsider in the future.

reply_data.body: Thanks for doing this! One of my main "design directions" would be that it results into an svg that is "simple to parse by human". The consequences are: 1) use simple shapes; 2) not much overall detail; 3) not many new colors. At glance, I like this one (but probably with a different shape and color for the star on top of the tree): One thing to keep in mind are proportions and not to add too much extra space above the name. This will be used as a social preview, so text should be not much less readable. > To be honest, I'd love to see more people get involved. Designers are especially welcome to share their critiques! I'd rather not. It can get complicated quickly.
